title: Best habit app, hands-down
body: I’ve tried a lot of different apps + paper strategies over the years to track habits, and this app has been the best by a mile. It’s easy to set up and stick with, enjoyable to use and visually beautiful, flexible to my needs while keeping me accountable. One underrated excellent feature is that they give you fine-tuned control over the notifications you receive — probably the #1 reason I’ve deleted other habit apps was that they spammed me with a billion distracting notifications, but Not Boring doesn’t create this issue. Price is perfectly reasonable/well worth it. There’s only one minor feature I’d like them to add: I’d love if I could toggle on a “don’t skip 2” option in the settings - I.e. make it so that streaks are only considered “broken” if you miss 2 instances. But otherwise literally perfect.

title: Beautiful, but bad UX
body:
For the most part, I really like this app. There's no ads and the developers don't collect your data. The app is habit tracking in its simplest form. You just open the app and hold the button, no fluff. 

The sounds and haptics are great, giving you a small dose of dopamine every time you check something off. 

I have a handful of issues, though. First is there's a tight character limit on each habit. I found it hard to squeeze some of my habits in.

Second is I don't care for the cryptic messages you get with every check. Wish I could disable those.

Third and most importantly, the user experience is cumbersome. You have to swipe one at a time through every habit. At the end of every day, when I want to restart back at habit one, I have to swipe through 16 habits. That alone is enough for me to not want to use this app anymore.

Then you have the fact that every time you swipe to a different habit, it brings you back to the checkmark screen. So if I want to look at the calendar view for my habits, I have to swipe up twice to get to the calendar, swipe left to go to the next habit, swipe up twice to again get to the calendar, swipe left to go to the next habit, etc...

The worst part about this is, these issues aren't readily apparent from the free version when you only have two habits to look at. 

Finally, this is personal taste, but I don't like a single one of 10 skins you get with premium, which was a bummer.

title: Kind of life changing
body:
The thought and attention to detail that the developer put into this app is astounding. As you take each step toward your goal, it feels like you’re on an epic journey - full of small victories, unexpected setbacks, and hard won wisdom. The artwork and text that accompanies each level is well chosen to keep you motivated and help you appreciate the journey, not just the goal. 

I tried out the paid version on a whim and I can’t believe it was actually worth it, but for me it was genuinely helpful for staying on track. Thanks in no small part to this app, I’m meditating daily and well on my way to learning how to do an unsupported handstand. I’ve also cut back my doomscrolling dramatically, thanks to a “no Internet before breakfast” habit.

title: Has Potential!
body:
I am searching for a habit-tracking app that is easy to use, doesn't require a subscription, and doesn't force you to watch advertisements.

This application is by an independent creator and is 100% member-supported, meaning there are no advertisements (YAY!). A yearly subscription is $14.99, less than a quarter of the price for competitor habit trackers (BOO, subscription. YAY, it’s more affordable than most). 

Since I am looking for something that doesn’t require a subscription, it was a bummer to see that the widgets are only available to paid members. 

One improvement I’d like to see is tracking specific amounts until the habit is completed for the day. For example, I want to track my water consumption by measuring the ounces or glasses of water I drink, and then the habit is “complete” after X ounces are marked off as completed. 

I am going to give this application some more time to see if it fits my needs.

title: FEATURES TO ENHANCING THE GAME
body:
This habit tracker has a lot of potential to replacing any habit tracker on the AppStore but it still needs some work. I have some suggestions to improve it but it’s up to you guys (the people who use this app) if you want them added or not.

MY SUGGESTIONS:
Seeing one habit at a time is great but swiping the small names of the habits at the top makes navigating to other habits annoying and difficult. The best way to go about this is to make it so that we can quickly choose seeing all our habits in the day (a dashboard), then picking a habit to see it by itself to check it off the same way it is now. 

Adding a feature where after you see the piece you’ve added to your “base” by completing a habit it then transitions to the next habit in order by which you set them throughout the day.

Adding challenges and completing them gives you miniature trophies that you can view in the trophy room. The challenges can be something like keeping a constant habit streak for 20 days and you win a a trophy called ‘persistent’ that gets added to the trophy room. Then you can add trophies with tiers like the 20 day one being bronze and keeping a streak for 365 days gives you a trophy that could be called ‘unstoppable’ in the legendary or mythic tier.

Adding a rank feature that puts in different tiers based off of how many habits you have as well as how many days you’ve completed puts you in a different rank. Kinda like in the game apex; rookie, bronze, silver, gold, diamond, platinum, master, and Apex predator.

Contact me for questions or more suggestions, thank you for listening.

It’s a fascinating psychological reinforcement that‘s well designed and effective.

title: Great habit tracker, overpriced
body:
Habits is one of the best habit trackers I’ve ever used. It’s beautiful, fun, encouraging, and the satisfaction of getting another level makes it so I don’t need 50 notifications a day to open it (and it doesn’t send you a ton like other apps.)

The big problem is it’s subscription. It’s $70/year if you want any decent “skins”, the cheaper tier doesn’t include any fun ones. That’s way too much for a habits app.

Theoretically it includes 3 other apps, but this is the only good one. The other apps included are extremely over-designed and underpowered, an example of when you have designers over following trends who’ve never used the app they’re building. The calculator app is great until it lags while you type a 3 digit number, the weather app doesn’t look as good or act as well as the stock weather app that’s free or something like Carrot weather which is cheaper. The timer app has no live activity support, doesn’t support hours, and is just all around unusable. Out of all the apps, this one feels like the devs never opened a timer before in their life.

Anyway, great habits app, shouldn’t cost as much.

Habit tracker. Other habit trackers have too much other gunk like blogs or media that don’t actually add any value. This app thoughtfully restrains the UI  complexity of adding tasks. This app is also stunningly beautiful with satisfying animations and haptics coupled with inspiring narrative progression— gives a good positive feedback loop to completing habits. It’s the sort of thing that I would give 6 stars, because even without this level of polish, this would be an excellent habit building tool. Subscription price is reasonable, and actually cheaper than the previous habit tracker I was using so that’s a win.

title: Fantastic app with two flaws
body:
I absolutely love the artistry and interface. One of the flaws (biggest one) is not having cross device support. I understand you’d have to have a database and hold user data for this which would cost you instead of holding all the data locally on the user’s device. I’d suggest adding another pricing tier to add this feature. I’d pay it. I use my MacBook, 2 iPads, and iPhone interchangeably and it’s frustrating not being able to track habits from different devices. Add this feature and you’ll have 5 stars. On top of being able to seamlessly track habits across devices (without having to click a button like restore), it would be great to access skins this way as well instead of unlocking them on each device. Second flaw is not having a landscape view.

Bonus extra work: create icon sets to match the artistry of the app and wallpapers. Jump onboard iOS16 developer beta and create some new Lock Screen skins. Create a daily task manager app. You’ll be making booku bucks. :) just a suggestion.

title: Great Concept. Poor Usability.
body:
The tone of the interface has such a fun attitude that it’s such a nice break from the mundane habit / tasks apps out there. Completing a task is such a blast.

However, once you actually try to use it, this app falls apart. Ambiguous icons without labels, unintuitive swipes that reveal different views (but also accidentally rotating the 3D trophy to no end), no consolidated list / calendar view of all of your habits, focusing the entire app experience on building a 3D model (how does this help?) etc.

It’s a shame - this is a great experimental app with some of the best micro-animations & interactions of any app. Too bad it didn’t seem to focus on what the user actually needs to do.

Literally EVERYTHING I do now related to creating the habits feels like a game now! I almost look forward to completing it every day, and the force feedback of the app is just so satisfying. I could do it all day if I could.
